_comment: TEMPLATE. A file-backed store using the same path shape as Vault, for the
one case where it is legitimate: an application whose credentials are
genuinely public, such as a public demo site. Anything else belongs in
LocalSecretStore serves only the selecting profile's own credential root,
so entries for one target can never be read by another.
Path shape matches Vault KV v2: <root>/<accountType>/<role>/<n>.
_toolshop: Public demo credentials, printed on the application's own documentation.
They go through the `secrets` fixture anyway: the moment one target is
allowed to bypass it, the lint rule stops being enforceable.
These credentials are not dependable, and that is a property of the
target rather than of this file. Over one onboarding session:
- customer@ and customer2@ were locked out (HTTP 423) by this suite's
own wrong-password specs; the lock outlives the run.
- customer3@ stopped accepting its documented password, because the
credentials are published and anyone may change them.
- an account the suite registered for itself was wiped within twenty
minutes: the deployment reseeds on a schedule, which also restored
customer@ and rotated every product id in the catalogue.
The reseed is why customer@ is usable again. It is also why the profile
declares sharedEnvironment: true, why nothing here transcribes an id, and
why the honest home for this pack is a local docker compose deployment.
